This guide is for anyone hosting a game night who wants to pick a game that
suits their group. It shows you how to install the package, launch the app,
use its controls and read what it tells you.


## Install and launch

Install gamenight from GitHub, then launch the app:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-noormoolji17")

gamenight::run_app()
```

The app opens in your viewer or browser. It uses the game data that comes with
the package, so it works without an internet connection.

## The question the app answers

> For my group's size and ages, how much time do we need to allow to play a
> really well-rated game?

There is no single "best game". The best game for two people with half an hour
is completely different from the best game for eight people with an evening,
so the app lets you describe *your* group.

## Using the controls

The sidebar on the left describes your group:

- **How many people are playing?** Only games that can be played with exactly
  this many people are shown.
- **How much time do you have?** Games whose typical playing time is longer
  than this are left out. This is the most important control; as one can  drag   it to see what extra time would unlock.
- **Age of the youngest player.** Uses the publisher's suggested minimum age.
  Leave it at 18 or more if everyone is an adult.
- **Only include games rated by at least…** A rating from a handful of people
  is less reliable. The default of 1,000 people keeps well-known games; lower
  it to see more obscure ones.
- **Only cooperative games.** Tick this if your group would rather work as a
  team than compete.

## Reading the results

The app gives three outputs, from quickest to most detailed:

1. **What fits your group.** A sentence telling you how many games fit, the
   best-rated one, and whether allowing another 30 minutes would get you a
   better game.
2. **Rating against playing time.** Each point is a game your group could
   play. Solid red dots fit in your time; hollow grey circles need more time.
   The dashed line is your time limit. Look for points near the top: if the
   best grey circles sit just to the right of the line, a little more time
   would get you a noticeably better game.
3. **Top 10 games that fit.** The best matches, with a link to each game on
   BoardGameGeek.

Ratings are BoardGameGeek's *adjusted* rating out of 10. It pulls games with
few ratings towards the average, so a game rated highly by only a handful of
people can't top the list.

## A worked example

Say six friends are coming over. With 45 minutes to spare:

```{r}
library(gamenight)

short <- find_games(players = 6, max_minutes = 45)
nrow(short)
head(short[, c("name", "playing_time", "rating")], 3)
```

If they can stay for 90 minutes instead:

```{r}
long <- find_games(players = 6, max_minutes = 90)
nrow(long)
head(long[, c("name", "playing_time", "rating")], 3)
```

Doubling the time adds `r nrow(long) - nrow(short)` games, and the best
option improves from `r short$name[1]` (`r round(short$rating[1], 1)`) to
`r long$name[1]` (`r round(long$rating[1], 1)`). The app shows this trade-off
as you drag the time slider.

## When nothing fits

Some groups have very few options. For ten players including a six-year-old,
with only 15 minutes:

```{r}
find_games(players = 10, max_minutes = 15, youngest_age = 6)
```

No games fit. Instead of an empty screen, the app shows a yellow message
naming the quickest game that suits the group and how much time it needs, so
you know what to change. If the number of players is left blank or is outside
1 to 20, the app asks you to enter a valid number.

## Things to keep in mind

- Ratings come from BoardGameGeek users, who are enthusiasts and tend to rate
  longer, more complex games highly. A casual group might enjoy shorter games
  more than the ratings suggest.
- The data is a snapshot from January 2022, so newer games are missing.
- "Board games" here means any tabletop game on BoardGameGeek, including card,
  dice and party games.
- Playing times and minimum ages are the publisher's suggestions. Your group
  may be faster or slower.
  

The data comes from [BoardGameGeek](https://boardgamegeek.com), via Kaggle and
[TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2022/2022-01-25).
See `?games` for details.
